issues.legal_issue: Criminal proceedings against a person who received a lease may be quashed when the complaint, accepted in full, does not allege facts showing that the person knew of or participated in the alleged fabrication of title documents.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that a family member fabricated documents claiming ownership of disputed inherited property and then leased it to the accused.
The accused’s alleged role was limited to receiving the lease; the complaint did not allege facts showing that he knew the lessor was not the sole owner or colluded in fabricating the documents.
The dispute over inheritance and the validity of the documents was already before civil courts, including in a pending partition suit.
The police final report stated that the investigation had found no material showing a conspiracy.
issues.conclusion: The complaint and supporting material disclosed no prima facie case against the accused, so the proceedings against him were quashed as an abuse of process.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, proceedings may be quashed where the allegations, even if accepted at face value, do not prima facie make out an offence or where the uncontroverted allegations and supporting evidence disclose no offence, as stated in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal. Where the validity of an alleged will is already before a civil court, a criminal prosecution based merely on the allegation that the will is forged should not proceed while that question is being determined; Sardool Singh v. Nasib Kaur. A disputed inheritance and title claim is to be resolved in the appropriate civil proceeding, and the court should avoid permitting unsupported criminal allegations against a person whose involvement is not shown.

rule.if: criminal_quashing_application and allegations_taken_at_face_value and accused_role_limited_to_receiving_lease and complaint_lacks_knowledge_or_collusion_allegations and forgery_attributed_to_another_actor and civil_title_suit_pending and investigation_found_no_conspiracy_material

predicates.criminal_quashing_application: A person asks a court to quash criminal proceedings against them.
predicates.allegations_taken_at_face_value: The court assesses the complaint on the assumption that its allegations are true.
predicates.accused_role_limited_to_receiving_lease: The complaint alleges that the accused received a lease but does not describe other participation in the alleged wrongdoing.
predicates.complaint_lacks_knowledge_or_collusion_a: The complaint does not set out facts showing that the accused knew of the alleged fraud or colluded in it.
predicates.forgery_attributed_to_another_actor: The complaint attributes the creation of the allegedly fabricated title documents to another person.
predicates.civil_title_suit_pending: A civil proceeding is pending to determine the disputed ownership or validity of the documents.
predicates.investigation_found_no_conspiracy_materi: The investigation found no material supporting an alleged conspiracy.

issues.definition: When a person seeking quashing is alleged only to have received a lease, the complaint and investigation show no facts connecting that person to another actor’s alleged fabrication, and the title dispute is pending in civil court, the criminal proceedings against that person are quashed.

issues.legal_issue: Criminal proceedings may be quashed against persons whose only apparent connection to the transaction is their employment by an entity involved in it or their attestation of a document, when no material implicates them in an offence.
material_facts: The complainant challenged the quashing of proceedings against a company and its officers or employees, as well as two persons who had attested the lease document.
The High Court found no material against the company’s officers or employees.
The two attesting witnesses had been implicated only because they witnessed the document.
The Supreme Court found no merit in the complainant’s appeals and upheld the quashing.
issues.conclusion: The complainant’s appeals were dismissed, leaving the proceedings quashed against the company’s officers or employees and the attesting witnesses.
issues.legal_principle: Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure permits quashing where the allegations and available material do not disclose an offence against the accused. Under the principles in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, proceedings may be quashed when the allegations, even if accepted, do not make out a case, or when the uncontroverted allegations and supporting material disclose no offence.

rule.if: complainant_appeal_against_quashing and ((accused_are_employees_or_officers and no_material_of_offence) or (accused_are_attesting_witnesses and no_material_of_offence))

predicates.complainant_appeal_against_quashing: A complainant appeals against an order quashing criminal proceedings against the accused.
predicates.accused_are_employees_or_officers: The accused are officers or employees of an entity involved in the transaction.
predicates.no_material_of_offence: The complaint and available material do not implicate the accused in an offence.
predicates.accused_are_attesting_witnesses: The accused are alleged to have witnessed or attested the document at issue.

issues.definition: When a complainant challenges the quashing of proceedings against employees or officers, or against attesting witnesses, and no material implicates those accused in an offence, the quashing is upheld.
